title: Sky Courier: Storm Run
premise: A small glowing sky courier craft races along a stormy aerial route, collecting energy rings to keep its storm buffer alive while dodging barriers and lightning strikes.
interaction_model: Single-input endless steering game controlled by touch or pointer drag; the craft auto-advances while the player only moves horizontally and taps to restart after failure.
objective: Survive as long as possible, travel the farthest distance, avoid hazards, and collect energy rings to restore health.
progression: The run begins immediately, speed gradually increases over time, hazards and pickups spawn continuously, low health triggers warning feedback, and the session ends when health reaches zero before allowing an instant restart.
theme: Arcade sci-fi sky delivery through dangerous storm corridors.
mood: Energetic, breezy, bright, slightly tense, and replay-driven.
likely_audience: players who enjoy dodge-and-collect survival loops
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is an endless survival runner with lateral steering, procedural hazards, and health-based endurance.
High confidence that distance is the primary score metric shown to the player.
Moderate confidence that the player avatar is meant to read as a courier craft or drone rather than a humanoid character.
Moderate confidence that the game belongs most strongly to endless runner / lane-runner-adjacent categories rather than shooter or racing categories.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished mobile-friendly browser arcade game called "Sky Courier: Storm Run" where the player controls a small glowing sky courier craft on a full-screen canvas and steers it left and right with touch or mouse drag while it automatically rushes forward through a stormy aerial corridor. The goal is to survive as long as possible and push a visible distance meter higher while managing a health-like "storm buffer" bar. Spawn three main object types from the top of the screen: collectible golden energy rings that restore health and give satisfying positive feedback, solid cargo barriers that deal heavy damage on collision, and telegraphed lightning strikes that first warn the player with an indicator before becoming active damaging hazards. Make the world feel like an endless runner even if movement is mostly lateral: use a scrolling road-or-flight-lane illusion, center striping, drifting clouds, particles, increasing speed over time, and quick reaction gameplay. Include arcade juice such as glowing effects, particle bursts, danger overlays when health is low, punchy sound effects, looping action music, optional vibration on supported devices, and small animated reaction visuals for collecting and crashing. Present a clean HUD with distance and health, then show a stylish game-over card with the final distance and a single restart button. Keep the tone bright, futuristic, and storm-charged, with short replayable runs and easy one-handed controls.
